title: The Almost Mixtape
premise: Mirabel Villalobos has perfected invisibility at Westfield High, but when debate coach Ms. Okafor pairs him with his nemesis, Theo Brandt, for a semester-long project documenting the school's quietly buried scholarship scandal, his head-down strategy collapses. As the two rivals build an unlikely mixtape of testimony from students the system failed, Mirabel must choose between protecting his undocumented best friend Camila and exposing the vice principal whose 'charitable' scholarship fund funneled money to donors' kids. In the end, Mirabel loses the state championship on purpose, wins the argument that matters by playing their evidence at the spring showcase, and discovers that belonging isn't something you earn quietly — it's something you claim out loud.
about_author: D. M. Sterling is the pen name of a former high school debate coach who spent seven years watching teenagers argue brilliantly about everything except themselves. Sterling writes from a small apartment full of half-labeled mixtapes and unfinished rebuttals.

chapters.title: Locker Shut, Head Down
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. We meet a debate champion who deliberately loses the final round to avoid attention, while at home his parents' arguments drown out everything. Establish his invisibility rules and his fierce loyalty to Camila, whose scholarship application just mysteriously vanished. Emotional beat: the ache of being unheard in your own house.

chapters.title: Assigned to the Enemy
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Ms. Okafor announces semester pairs for a 'documentary of an injustice' project — and pairs Mirabel with Theo Brandt, the smug rival who beat him freshman year. Their first meeting in the library is pure friction, until Theo lets slip he's been investigating the scholarship fund too, for his own reasons. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity cracking old contempt.

chapters.title: The First Voice on the Tape
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The boys interview a former student, Marisol, who lost her scholarship when the fund was 'restructured.' Her testimony is the mixtape's first track. Mirabel realizes Camila's vanished application fits a pattern. Emotional beat: the chill of discovering the injustice is a system, not an accident.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. We learn why Theo cares: his older brother was a victim of the same fund years ago, and Theo's perfectionism is penance. The rivals negotiate ground rules — no going to the administration, no involving families. Mirabel breaks rule two immediately by telling Camila nothing. Emotional beat: guilt disguised as protection.

chapters.title: Static
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Debate season heats up and Mirabel is winning again, which means visibility he can't afford. Vice Principal Hargrove starts noticing the boys' project and offers Mirabel a private 'mentorship' — a bribe wrapped in kindness. Camila, sensing his secrecy, pulls away. Emotional beat: the loneliness of keeping two secrets.

chapters.title: Track Six: Camila's Voice
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Camila discovers the mixtape and, hurt that Mirabel hid it, demands to be on it — her testimony, her choice. Recording her, Mirabel hears the case against Hargrove become undeniable. Theo and Mirabel have their first real fight about whether to go public before they have proof. Emotional beat: loyalty and truth pulling in opposite directions.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Hargrove escalates: a full-ride scholarship for Theo, his brother's name quietly cleared, if the project 'stays academic.' Theo almost takes it. Mirabel finds out and calls him a coward — the same word Theo once threw at him. Their partnership shatters two weeks before the state championship and the spring showcase deadline. Emotional beat: betrayal cutting deepest from an ally.

chapters.title: What the Trophy Is For
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Alone, Mirabel prepares for states and realizes he's been debating his whole life to avoid the real argument. He visits Marisol and Camila, apologizes, and asks their permission to play the mixtape at the showcase — with names attached. Camila says yes, but only if he stops hiding too. Emotional beat: courage as a decision, not a feeling.

chapters.title: The Round That Doesn't Count
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, climax part one. At the state final, facing Theo on opposite teams again, Mirabel deliberately concedes the championship mid-rebuttal, telling the auditorium the argument that matters is happening Friday at the showcase. Theo, stunned, walks out of the awards ceremony and joins him backstage. Emotional beat: losing the wrong prize to win the right one.

chapters.title: Side B
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, climax and resolution. At the spring showcase, the boys play the mixtape — every voice, every name, Camila last. Hargrove is suspended pending investigation; an independent fund is announced with Marisol and Camila's families at the table. Mirabel goes home and, for the first time, asks his parents to listen. Final beat: he presses play on a new mixtape titled for the people who finally heard him.
